title: Graceful payload-slimming & regional admission orchestrator
creator: Aisha Verma
description:
Problem: During cross-region incidents and tail latency storms we need finer-grained load-shedding that reduces load without dropping the vast majority of requests. Existing approaches at Redwood focus on lane-based priority admission and token-budget shedding. We need an operator-friendly mechanism that: 1) trims request payloads (payload-slimming) according to safe heuristics so the runtime spends fewer tokens, 2) integrates with admission control to prefer routing to a healthy region or degraded path, and 3) cooperates with circuit-breakers to enable fast fallback and staged recovery.

Goal: Deliver a production-ready 'Payload Slimming + Regional Admission Orchestrator' that reduces GPU token load and preserves SLOs for high-value tenants by combining request-slimming heuristics, staged admission policies, and region-aware routing. This feature should be configurable per-tenant and per-route, have observable metrics, and include a runbook for operators.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Incoming requests can be annotated with a slim profile that applies: field removal, context window truncation based on semantics, and structured-output collapse. 2) Orchestrator can route requests to an alternate region when local latency or capacity thresholds are breached, using progressive passback (attempt local -> slim -> remote) without changing client-visible model version. 3) Circuit-breaker signals (error rate, queue depth, tail latency) trigger immediate slimming + optional region passback within 200ms of detection. 4) System exposes per-tenant metrics: tokens_saved, slim_invocations, passback_rate, successful_passbacks, and fallout_count. 5) No silent correctness regressions: for a representative set of prompts, accuracy loss must be < 3% when slimming is applied (measured via nightly evaluation harness).
design_notes:
High-level design:
- Admission orchestrator sits as a short-circuit layer on the request-path, before batching and kernel selection. It evaluates local load signals (queue length, 99th latency, token credits) and tenant affinity settings.
- Payload slimming is implemented as a set of transformer-friendly heuristics and a small classifier that decides which sections of a request can be trimmed safely. Slim profiles are composed of: (a) remove optional `metadata` keys, (b) compress long context fields by summarization, (c) collapse structured arrays to top-N entries, (d) truncate long user-provided context using importance scoring (TF-IDF-like with recency bias), (e) drop non-essential tool-call contexts when fallback is available.
- Slimming runs synchronously and returns a trace header telling callers what changed. The orchestrator maintains a short-lived cache of trimmed prefixes to increase hit rate for repeated prompts.
- Regional passback strategy: local -> slim_local -> remote_primary -> remote_slim. Routing decisions respect tenant routing policy (prefer_local, prefer_remote, failover-only).
- Circuit breakers: hybrid (rate + latency + error) with state machine (Closed, Probe, Open). On transition to Probe/Open, orchestrator toggles slimming aggressive profiles and increases remote passback thresholds.

Trade-offs considered:
- CPU vs GPU: slimming consumes CPU (summarization/salience compute) but reduces GPU time. We budget 10ms avg CPU per request for slimming to save multiple tens of ms on GPU in most cases.
- Consistency: Structured outputs can change shape; we prefer to return a slimmed-but-valid schema and include headers for callers to detect degraded fidelity.
- Complexity: Adding a classifier increases surface area; initial rollout can gate classifier and default to simple heuristics.
implementation_tasks: Add orchestrator component in front of runtime batching pipeline
Implement three default slim profiles: conservative, balanced, aggressive
Integrate lightweight importance scoring library (C++/Rust binding) for context truncation
Expose tenant config API for slim profiles and passback policy
Wire circuit-breaker signals from metrics pipeline to orchestrator (pub/sub)
Add observability: slim_invocations, tokens_saved, passback_rate, passback_latency
Create e2e test harness against production-like workload to measure accuracy delta
Add tracing headers and explainability payload documenting slimmed fields
Create operator runbook and dashboard widgets in Console
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag: off by default. 2) Internal dogfood: enable for non-critical tenants in us-west-2 with conservative profile for 1 week. 3) Canary: enable for 5 mid-size customers with monitoring and alerts. 4) Gradual ramp to 'balanced' for customers on failover plan. 5) Post-rollout: run weekly accuracy regression checks and keep conservative profile for any tenant failing tests.
test_plan: Unit tests for heuristics + classifier. Integration tests verifying correct routing sequence (local->slim->remote). Load test simulating spike with and without slimming to measure token savings and P99 latency. Nightly eval comparing answers on 3 curated prompt sets; assert <3% accuracy drop. Chaos run: trigger region outage and validate passback success rate and SLA preservation.
runbook: Operator steps when passback_rate spikes: 1) Check orchestrator health in Console, 2) Review tokens_saved and p99_latency graphs, 3) If slim_invocations are high and accuracy alerts firing, flip tenant-level profile to conservative or disable slimming, 4) If remote regions failing to accept passbacks, escalate to networking oncall and failover the region routing to alternative remote pool.
observability_requirements:
- Metrics: tokens_saved (counter), slim_invocations (counter), passback_rate (ratio), passback_latency (histogram), passback_success (counter)
- Traces: end-to-end trace where slim profile decision and changed fields are annotated
- Alerts: passback_failure_rate > 5% over 5m, tokens_saved drop indicates slimming not triggering when expected
notes: Initial prototype demonstrated ~28% median token reduction on chat-style histories by collapsing system messages and summarizing long user contexts. Some customers showed increased hallucination risk on aggressive profiles — hence conservative default. We will surface slimmed field diffs to integrators for debugging.
